definitions.explanation: The area or direction that is lower in position. Used for physical location (below something) and for abstract concepts like downward trends in data or economics.

examples.japanese: {画面|がめん}の{下方|かほう}にボタンがある。
examples.english: There is a button in the lower part of the screen.

examples.japanese: {業績|ぎょうせき}{予想|よそう}が{下方|かほう}{修正|しゅうせい}された。
examples.english: The earnings forecast was revised downward.

examples.japanese: {崖|がけ}の{下方|かほう}に{小|ちい}さな{集落|しゅうらく}が{見|み}えた。
examples.english: A small settlement was visible below the cliff.

notes:
A formal word for indicating downward direction or the lower portion of something. Particularly common in written language, news reports, and technical/financial contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {下方|かほう}{修正|しゅうせい}: downward revision (often of economic forecasts)
- {下方|かほう}に{向|む}かう: to head downward
- {下方|かほう}{圧力|あつりょく}: downward pressure
- {画面|がめん}の{下方|かほう}: lower part of the screen

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {上方|じょうほう}: upper part; upward — the antonym
- {下部|かぶ}: lower section; base — emphasizes the structural bottom part
- {下|した}: below; under — everyday, informal equivalent
- {以下|いか}: below; less than — used for quantities and rankings

USAGE:
Do not confuse with {家宝|かほう} (family treasure), which has the same pronunciation but different kanji.
